olivia: Quick question — running into weird behavior with session reservation + queued requests when we soft-cancel an in-flight streaming call.
samir: Can you sketch the symptoms? Is this on Dedicated or Hosted? :eyes:
olivia: Hosted. Sequence: client opens streaming request -> gateway reserves a session slot -> downstream stalls -> we soft-cancel (send trailer) -> client retries -> new request gets queued but the old reservation never releases, so it later consumes capacity and causes duplicate processing.
jia: yikes. Do you mean the reservation lease isn't cleared on soft-cancel (vs hard abort)?
olivia: Exactly. Logs show lease state stays "reserved" for ~30s then eventually times out, but in the interim a retry is scheduled and attaches to a queued slot. Observed on shorter backends with bursty latency.
tom: Paste logs? Could be lease vs queue lifecycle mismatch.
olivia: Logs:

```
[2026-03-12T10:21:05Z] proxy: session=sr-8a3 reserved -> client-stream-start
[2026-03-12T10:21:20Z] backend: stall detected -> soft_cancel_sent
[2026-03-12T10:21:20Z] proxy: sent trailer (soft_cancel)
[2026-03-12T10:21:22Z] client: retry initiated -> queued position=4
[2026-03-12T10:21:55Z] proxy: lease sr-8a3 expired -> session closed
[2026-03-12T10:21:56Z] queued req attached -> backend processed same logical request
```

samir: Hmm. Two possible classes: 1) soft-cancel doesn't release the reservation (intentional so downstream can finish) 2) retry policy doesn't observe that reservation and will queue a new slot. Need coordination.
jia: For safety we currently guarantee at-most-once backend dispatch only for hard-aborts; soft-cancel is a graceful signal so it's allowed to race, but that causes dupes for idempotent-unfriendly endpoints.
tom: Could we make retries consult a reservation index keyed by idempotency token / session id and prefer to reattach to an existing session if recent soft-cancel was sent? That obviates queuing a fresh slot.
olivia: Proposal: add a short rendezvous window (configurable, default 5s) after soft-cancel where the gateway will accept reattach attempts referencing the original reservation token. Outside window we treat as new request and enqueue normally. Also ensure the reservation header is cleared on hard-abort only.
samir: What about old clients that don't send reattach token? They'll queue as today; risk remains. But we should at least avoid double-allocating when token present.
jia: Implementation note: we have an existing lease table with states {reserved, draining, closed}. Add substate "soft-drain" with TTL. Retrying requests can include header `X-Session-Reclaim: <lease-id>` and we check soft-drain table.
tom: Two tradeoffs:
- Complexity: more bookkeeping and longer-lived metadata in frontdoor.
- Cost: small memory for soft-drain index; benefits for idempotency-sensitive paths.

olivia: Edge cases: what if the downstream actually completes after soft-cancel and produces side-effects and the reattach then causes duplicate side-effect? We should tie reattach only to requests marked idempotent or to clients that attach idempotency keys.
samir: Agree. Default policy: only allow reattach if request had `Idempotency-Key` or session was created via `interactive=true` flag (internal opt-in).
jia: We also need metrics: soft_drains_created, reattaches_succeeded, reattaches_failed, reattach_time_ms histogram.
tom: And add telemetry to show queue length delta when soft-cancel occurs to measure benefit.

olivia: Secondary idea: when soft-cancel is sent, proactively decrement your queue admission credit for new requests from same client until lease expires — reduces churn. But that's more invasive.
samir: I prefer the rendezvous window + header approach. Low-risk, incremental.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy to prod-edge cluster-7 scheduled at 2026-03-15T02:00Z
olivia: I'll draft an RFC follow-up with API sketch and small sequence diagram. Will include migration plan for backward clients (no-op) and metrics.
tom: Add a small e2e test: simulate backend stall + soft cancel + immediate retry w/ and w/o Idempotency-Key.
jia: Also test burst scenario where many clients soft-cancel at once, ensure soft-drain index GC keeps up.
samir: Sounds good. If you want I'll pair on the prototype.
olivia: Thanks — will post RFC link when ready. :thumbsup:
